label: original-phase input from a token set (j,v,1,n,y,a,k,c) after a u/b/p/g/w/d/s/q token was seen
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase (94.5% of activation mass); it never fires at t=0 and is rare at the delimiter and in the copy phase. Two things drive it. The current input matters: j, v, 1, n, y, a, k and c have 2.2-4.1x lift, e and h are weaker, and l and m are low. The prefix matters too: rates are much higher when earlier inputs include u, b, p, g, w, d, s or q, and first_tok u has 3.1x lift. Rate also rises with position (orig_idx 5-7 has about 3.5x lift). The top activations are all of this kind, e.g. a j or v input late in a sequence that starts with u or b. Plain conjunctions of these conditions get dev F1 of about 0.5 (precision 0.43, recall 0.58, mass recall 0.74), so the unit looks like a graded sum of these cues rather than a crisp rule. It misses lower-magnitude firings on other tokens and has many false positives on the listed tokens. Weak in the copy phase (about 4% of mass, mostly when outputting u).
